events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph first.** Rating: **3 (good)**.
- **Grand Haven, Muskegon, and South Haven are all about average, rated 2.** Grand Haven's rating is a weak positive because its report didn't rate the fishing.
- **Fish 110–120 ft of water at St. Joseph and South Haven, and 80–150 ft at Grand Haven and Muskegon.** Run lines about 60–100 ft down.
- **Use spoons (orange or green, or glow) and green or yellow meat rigs.** At St. Joseph, rotators and flies also took fish.

## Why

- St. Joseph is the only port where the latest report rated boat fishing good, and it said spoons caught most of the fish.
- The latest reports from all four ports describe a similar pattern: fish around 60–120 ft down, with spoons and meat rigs working.
- I'd expect the lake to be warm (about 74–75 F at the buoys) and salmon to hold deeper than the surface, which is why the 60–100 ft range matters.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2023-07-26, six days before today)
- St. Joseph (2023-07-26): "Salmon anglers continued to have good success. … The most consistent water seemed to be around 120 feet. … Spoons were catching most of the fish, but rotators and flies were catching fish as well." Rated 3 (good).
- Grand Haven (2023-07-26): "Boat anglers were catching a mix bag of salmon and trout in 80 to 140 feet of water… Salmon were caught 60 to 120 feet down on orange or green spoons. … Yellow or green meat rigs worked well." Not rated.
- Muskegon (2023-07-26): "Boat anglers were finding the salmon action to be fair. … The best action was 60 to 100 down in 90 to 150 feet of water." Rated 2 (average).
- South Haven (2023-07-26): "Salmon anglers continued to have decent fishing. … The best water was around 110 feet of water. … Rotators and flies and meat rigs performed the best." Rated 2 (average).
- Trend: the Grand Haven and Muskegon reports from 2023-07-19 were rated 3 and 1, so the ratings have moved around week to week.

**Past seasons:** I didn't pull earlier-season comparisons because the latest reports are recent enough.

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2023-08-01, not live data)
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 75 F, South Haven 74 F, Grand Haven and Muskegon 72 F.
- Satellite surface water near the piers (GLSEA): about 73–75 F, roughly flat over the week.
- Wind that week averaged 6–7 mph, with gusts to 27–32 mph at all four ports. Upwelling-favoring wind was 30 h at St. Joseph over 7 days, but only 4 h in the last 3 days.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the conditions data is a summary of the week before today, not live readings.
- The surface is about 74–75 F, above the 52–58 F range that Chinook prefer (NY DEC general guidance). The cold layer should be deeper, but I had no modeled cold-layer depth for this week, so I can't give a depth for it.
- Grand Haven's report was not rated, so its 2 is a judgment, not a DNR rating.
- Gusts reached about 30 mph that week. For a small boat, check the forecast before going out and use the pier or river if it's rough.

## Sources

- Latest reports (2023-07-26): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3675eed
- Earlier context (2023-07-19): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
